articleTitle: A Single-Switch Single-Inductor High Step-Up DC-DC Converter with Single-Input and Dual-Output Ports
abstract: This study introduces an innovative configuration for a dual-output high-voltage DC-DC circuit. In applications such as light-emitting diode (LED) drivers, single-input dual-output structures (SIDO) offer superior performance compared to traditional structures, eliminating the need for two separate conventional DC-DC circuits. However, SIDO is constrained by the requirement for multiple switches, resulting in higher switching losses and diminished efficiency. The salient merits of this topology include diminished voltage stress on power switches and diodes, common ground availability, and enhanced efficiency. Additionally, the diminished voltage stresses enable the use of lower-rated semiconductors, leading to cost and volume savings. To validate the theoretical propositions, a practical implementation of a 250W converter with a 50 kHz operational frequency, 20V input voltage, and load voltages of 100V and 40V has been carried out in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Robust Wireless Power Transfer by Self-Oscillating Controlled Inverter and Double-D Pads
abstract: Inductive wireless power transmission (IWPT) for mobile devices like electric vehicles (EVs) requires high efficiency and power stability. A resilient IWPT system is demonstrated in this paper with double-D pads (DDP) serving as the transmitter (Tr) and receiver (Re) with a self-oscillating controlled inverter to maintain constant output power and transmission efficiency regardless of variation in inductive coupling within a defined region, with no communication or control circuitry on the Re side. The proposed compact DDP-DDP inductive coupler with a single identical coil on both the Tr and Re pads provides a resilient IWPT system with up to a 20 cm transmission distance, up to 12 cm horizontal offset at a 20 cm transmission distance, and limited degrees of angular offset around the Z-axis between the Tr and Re that can tolerate coupling variations and achieve stable 1-kW output power with 92% steady transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: A New High gain Transformerless DC-DC Converter with Low Voltage Stress on Power Switches
abstract: In this article, a DC-DC step-up voltage topology for specific applications is presented. The propounded non-isolated configuration has merits such as achieving a high energy conversion rate with a low duty cycle and reducing voltage stress on the power switches. The theoretical analysis and operational modes of the circuit are discussed, and a comparative analysis with alternative boost DC-DC structures has been conducted to investigate the accuracy of its beneficial features, efficiency, and performance. To substantiate the theoretical discussions presented, the converter has been emulated in the PSCAD/EMTDC software, and the outcomes are described.

articleTitle: U-Net-Based Automotive Radar Target Detection and Recognition
abstract: In this paper, we have designed a CNN-based neural network, to detect targets using a FMCW radar more accurately than traditional methods. We have also shown that using this approach will enable us to not only detect targets but also it can categorize them, by their size, with high accuracy. Training of such a network requires a large amount of data, so one of the most challenging parts of this research was to simulate and generate suitable radar data to train the network. The detection rate of targets is reported for different SNRs and it increased by 40 percent on average, in comparison with CFAR methods.

articleTitle: High Performance Detector for Massive MIMO Systems Using an Adaptive Filtering Approach
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems are a critical technology in modern wireless communications, allowing increased data rates and link reliability. Owing to the increasing number of receivers and transmitters, finding a reliable, low-complexity, and accurate algorithm for data detection is a major issue. In this paper, an innovative method that melds the traditional minimum mean square error (MMSE) detector with an adaptive filter-based reconstruction algorithm is introduced. It is noteworthy that the MMSE detector error often exhibits sparsity, wherein only a few elements in the error vector are non-zero, representing incorrectly detected symbols. This inherent sparsity enables the utilization of efficient sparse recovery techniques for accurate error reconstruction. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method enhances performance without a substantial increase in computational overhead.

articleTitle: Design of Semi-Transparent Perovskite Solar Cells with Antireflection Coatings
abstract: A semitransparent perovskite solar cell is designed and simulated by replacing the metallic back-contact of a conventional perovskite solar cell with a transparent conducting material. To achieve the highest power conversion efficiency (PCE), three different materials as back-contacts, including ITO, IZO, and IHO, are exploited, Albedo sunlight is applied and consequently the results are compared. IOH is proved to offer the highest PCE. Finally, with IOH as back-contact, illuminating the incident light from both sides, and attaching two antireflection coatings to front and back-contacts with thicknesses of 100 and 80 nm, respectively, it is observed that the PCE offered by the semitransparent solar cell increases from 18.21% to 19.69%.

articleTitle: Efficient signal detection via compressive sensing in uplink massive MIMO systems
abstract: This article explores the topic of MIMO systems, which is a crucial technology in 5G wireless communications. While massive MIMO holds great promise, challenges encom-passing multi-antenna interference, channel estimation, and an-tenna correlation necessitate careful attention for acceptable performance. Optimal signal detection schemes, such as Maxi-mum Likelihood (ML), encounter exponential complexity growth with antenna and constellation size. This paper explores novel data detection techniques, notably sparse properties, within the framework of compressed sensing (CS) to enhance MIMO detection efficiency and reduce complexity. An iterative, and computationally efficient approach is proposed which converges to the benchmark method. Simulation results verify the efficacy and functionality of the proposed method. It will be shown that both the runtime and computational complexity are reduced while preserving high-performance.

articleTitle: A Centralized Adaptive PID Control of Telerehabilitation Systems Using Multi-Agent Systems Theory
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive PID control scheme for telerehabilitation systems, utilizing the theory of multi-agent systems. This control scheme consists of a PID term with which better synchronization for the position of telerehabilitation system operators is achieved. The structure of the proposed controller includes two adjustment matrices: a Laplacian matrix and a force adjustment matrix. The Laplacian matrix shows how the agents communicate to reach the desired position, and the force adjustment matrix shows the amount of force felt in the hands of each operator caused by the other operator's hands. Considering that in this control scheme, telerehabilitation systems are considered in the framework of multi-agent systems, it can be said that considering the self-intelligence between the agents and the communication graph between them, the separate design of the controller for each agent has been avoided. Also, with the appropriate selection of adjustment matrices, different rehabilitation scenarios can be implemented using this control scheme.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Power Transmission Lines Protection Against the Sub-Synchronous Resonance Using Thyristor-Based Reactive Power Compensation
abstract: In the contemporary landscape of power transmission, addressing compensation and voltage control poses a pivotal challenge for operators and managers in the power industry. Consequently, endeavors are being undertaken to optimize power transfer conditions in transmission lines through the integration of series compensation mechanisms while concurrently managing voltage and reactive power levels. Traditionally, the deployment of series capacitors is a prevalent practice due to its cost-effectiveness in regulating voltage and reactive power in transmission lines. Leveraging series capacitors not only enhances the maximum power transfer capacity but also bolsters the stability and voltage profile of the lines. Nevertheless, a drawback associated with utilizing series capacitors is the potential occurrence of subsynchronous resonance (SSR) within the network. To address this issue, this study proposes an innovative methodology aimed at mitigating SSR by devising an optimal controller for series capacitors with thyristor control (TCSC). The primary objective is to optimize voltage control and power transfer while minimizing the likelihood of subsynchronous resonance, a crucial aspect that has been overlooked in previous contemporary research endeavors. By introducing this novel approach, this research seeks to pioneer a comprehensive solution that integrates optimal controller design with TCSC technology to enhance system performance and reliability in power transmission networks.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Long Slot SIW Leaky Wave Antenna for Automotive Radar Application
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a leaky wave antenna utilizing substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) through various methodologies such as numerical analysis, HFSS, and simplified aperture function. The primary focus of the antenna design is its operation at 77 – 79 GHz, a commonly used frequency band for automotive radars. Initially, the mathematical foundation is discussed, followed by an explanation of two numerical approaches employed to determine the curve function of the slot. Given the lightweight and compact nature of radars operating in this frequency range, a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) was chosen as the waveguide type for the antenna design. Two alternative approaches have been employed to depict the slot on the waveguide, deviating from the conventional technique, and their respective performances have been evaluated. The initial approach replaces the slot with a series of holes, which serve as sampled points for a curve function. Conversely, the second approach maintains a rectangular shape for the slot with a narrow width, and instead of curving the slot, the waveguide vias are tapered to conform to the desired curve. The initial antenna configuration has achieved a gain of 4.3 dBi, a side lobe level (SLL) below 30 dB, and a bandwidth spanning 500 MHz Conversely, the subsequent design exhibits a gain of around 4 dBi, a SLL below 27 dB, and a bandwidth spanning 300 MHz.

articleTitle: Achieving a Wide Range of Voltage Gain in Three-Phase LLC Resonant Converter Using Hybrid Control of Variable Frequency and Variable Magnetizing Inductor
abstract: Resonant converters are utilized in industrial applications that prioritize power density and high efficiency. Among these converters, the three-phase LLC (TPLLC) resonant converter distinguishes itself with its remarkable attributes, encompassing high power density, low output current ripple, low conduction loss, and high efficiency. Just like the single-phase LLC (SPLLC) resonant converter, the frequency modulation technique is widely employed to control the output voltage in the TPLLC converter. However, using this converter in applications with broad input or output voltage ranges presents challenges in the design of magnetic components and gate drive circuits. To address these challenges, this article proposes a solution that combines magnetizing inductance control with frequency modulation. This combined approach enables achieving a broad range of voltage gain with minimal variations in switching frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sw</inf>). Additionally, due to the significant number of semiconductor elements in the TPLLC converter structure, controlling the magnetizing inductance can partially reduce circulating current, leading to lower conduction loss. This converter design is well-suited for applications that require extensive input or output voltage ranges, with adjustable input voltages ranging from 200 V to 400 V and output voltages ranging from 200 V to 450 V. Simulation results are also provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

Author Keywords: wide input and output voltage range

articleTitle: Improving ZVS Performance in Phase Shift LLC Converter using Variable Magnetizing Inductor for wide Input/Output Voltage Range
abstract: LLC converters face challenges in applications with a wide range of input voltages, as they need to vary the switching frequency (fsw) significantly to achieve the desired voltage gain. This leads to issues such as complicated design of magnetic elements and increased power dissipation. Phase-shift modulation (PSM) can solve these issues, but it has a drawback of losing zero-voltage switching (ZVS) in the lagging-leg switches when the phase-shift angle (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi)$</tex> is large, which results in high switching losses. Moreover, due to the large phase angle, there is a long period of time in one cycle where no energy is delivered to the load, which causes high circulation loss. To ensure ZVS operation at large phase angles, a combination of PSM and variable magnetizing inductor (MI) is proposed in this article. By optimally adjusting the value of the MI at all phase angles, not only ZVS operation are provided for lagging switches but also reduces circulating current, which ultimately reduces conduction losses. The Usefulness of the suggested control strategy is confirmed by simulation results.

Author Keywords: wide input and output voltage range

articleTitle: A Non-Isolated Extendable Common Grounded DC-DC Boost Converter for DC-Microgrid Applications
abstract: The DC-DC high step-up converters are vital sectors for interconnecting renewable energy sources to DC micro-grids and achieve to proper values of voltage for DC buses. A DC-DC non-isolated single switch converter is suggested in this paper. Being extendable while supplying common grounding feature are prominent exclusivities of this structure. The operation of the topology in continuous conduction modes is assessed and presented. The performance of the DC-DC boost converter is evaluated by comparing with similar other topologies. Moreover, dynamic performance is investigated. The accuracy of the presented topology is affirmed by simulating it using PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Forged Channel: A Breakthrough Approach for Accurate Parkinson's Disease Classification using Leave-One-Subject-Out Cross-Validation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel technique called “Forged Channel,” which aims to comprehensively represent EEG signals in order to achieve accurate classification of Parkinson's disease. The forged channel method prepares EEG signals in a manner that allows a deep learning model to effectively perceive all EEG channels within a single input. By employing this approach alongside a convolutional neural network, an impressive accuracy of 90.32% was achieved using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. This performance closely reflects real-world conditions, highlighting the superiority of our method compared to similar approaches.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an RF Module for UHF PD Measurement
abstract: Ultra high frequency (UHF) partial discharge (PD) measurement method outperforms the conventional method in some cases, such as better sensitivity, immunity against external disturbances, 3D localization and online monitoring. Despite the advantages of the UHF method, capturing PD in the frequency range of UHF is challenging. Firstly, UHF range measurement needs instruments with high sampling rate that raises the operating costs. Furthermore, the instruments of conventional PD measurement method are incompatible with UHF technique. To overcome the issue, an interface module is required to convert the UHF range of PD signals to lower frequencies within the range of the conventional method. This paper describes the development and evaluation of a down-converter module, followed by testing in a high-voltage laboratory to measure actual partial discharge (PD) occurrences within a transformer enclosure. The findings exhibit promising results in detecting PD events and generating phase-resolved partial discharge (PRPD) diagrams through the newly introduced interface module.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fault Tolerant Neural Control of Heterogeneous Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the stationary average consensus problem for second-order nonlinear multi-agent systems with heterogeneous unknown masses and uncertain nonlinear functions under balanced directed networks. Taking advantage of radial basis function neural networks, the unknown nonlinearity existed in the dynamics is counteracted. To deal with the unknown inertias, external disturbances, and actuator faults, adaptive control and sliding mode technique are utilized. By the theoretical analysis, it is shown that average consensus is reached provided that the network topology is balanced and contains a spanning tree. The proposed framework also guarantees consensus with the condition that the underlying network topology has a directed spanning tree. Finally, simulation results are given to better highlight the validity of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Study of an Improved Flux Reversal Permanent Magnet Outer-Rotor Motor
abstract: This paper analyzes two proposed flux reversal permanent magnet (FRPM) motors. The main motor, an improved FRPM (I-FRPM), was tested under no-load and full-load conditions. I-FRPM performs a higher torque density and low torque ripple structure. Using finite element methods (FEM), all curves are illustrated and compared to these two structures under fair conditions. This I-FRPM can be used in electric vehicle applications because it suggests a high torque density with minimal ripple motor structure.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Imitation of Human Actions for Autonomous Pick-and-Place Tasks
abstract: In robotics, attempts have been made to imitate movements through learning from demonstrations. There are two types of demonstration-based learning. Expert-based learning is expensive and time-consuming since it necessitates a paired observation-action procedure. Conversely, visual-based learning is more practical to collect and makes robots more adaptable to many kinds of tasks. But this problem still needs to be answered completely, and it's still a difficult assignment. This paper presents a comprehensive approach to replicating human actions in robots for object manipulation. As the main contribution of this paper, This research employs a deep learning methodology to allow robots to imitate human actions in grasping objects, utilizing human movement as a reference. A real dataset with 718 images and 142 videos has been collected in this paper. then The model is trained for object detection and object segmentation. To imitate human actions, a video of a person completing a task is recorded first. Following the subject's movements in the video allows for the extraction of the motion path. The robot then proceeds along the path that was extracted. The DPR impressively demonstrates the practical application, showcasing its capacity to imitate and execute human actions.

articleTitle: Primary-Side Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer System in Electric Vehicles
abstract: The Dynamic Wireless Charging (DWC) system offer a favorable solution to Electric Vehicle (EV) charging limitations, allowing for on-the-go charging. However, such systems usually require complex control strategies that involve communication between the primary and secondary systems. These requirements can result in higher costs, increased system complexity, and energy losses. In this paper, we present a new Primary-Side Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) method that operates based on the identification of load characteristics and which has been designed specifically for use in Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system for EVs to counteract variations in mutual inductance caused by coil movement. The NMPC is favored over conventional control techniques like the traditional Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) method thanks to its ability to anticipate future events and adjust control inputs proactively for robust and dynamic system response. The NMPC exhibits superior performance by yielding faster control response, decreased overshoot, and enhanced stability. Systematic simulations validate the proposed solution's efficacy.

articleTitle: An event-triggered distributed consensus information filter for target tracking in sensor networks
abstract: In this article, a distributed consensus information filter for sensor networks under the event-triggered strategy for tracking a target is proposed. According to this strategy in which the sensors only share their information with their neighbors at certain times, they can track their respective targets using the collected information. In addition, the event-trigger strategy is considered in order to reduce the required communication and an information gain matrix and an optimal distributed filter are created. Finally, a simulation example is presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Stabilizing Control System for Synchronizing a Biological Neuron Network Considering Electrical Autapse Effect
abstract: The synchronization of biological neurons plays a crucial role in processing and transmitting biological information and treatments. In this article, the main aim is to control the synchronization of a minimal neural network in a biological structure close to reality. The HMR model is chosen as the basic model after investigation of various neuron models. The effect of electrical autapse in the basic model is essential as shown by simulation. The error dynamics are calculated to achieve synchronization, and practically system is converted into an error or stabilization problem. A Lyapunov stability analysis is proposed to design a control system for neural network synchronization considering the autapse effect. The desired synchronization has been achieved by applying the control input while considering terms of biological details for a minimal neural network. Practically, these cases can directly assist the therapist in applying the appropriate control signal to achieve the desired dynamic and therapeutic behavior in the neural network.

articleTitle: Full Soft Switching Interleaved High Voltage Gain Converter for Renewable Energy Systems
abstract: High voltage gain converters are widely used between renewable energy resources and grid in renewable energy systems. Size, elements count, cost, input current ripple, and losses of such converters are desired to be low. To address these requirements, this article presents a novel high voltage gain interleaved converter with full soft switching operation which uses a few auxiliary elements. The auxiliary circuit in addition to providing soft switching function for all the components, contributes to enhancing the converter voltage gain. Furthermore, by exploiting interleaving technique, input current ripple is decreased in this converter. Besides, automatic current sharing between two interleaved phases is established. The operation principles as well as the simulation waveforms are given. Moreover, to show the effectiveness of the introduced converter, a comparison between the presented converter and some recently presented counterparts is provided.

articleTitle: Mountain Gazelle Optimized PID Controller for a MIMO System with External Disturbance
abstract: In this paper in order to control MIMO (Multi-Input Multi-Output) system against external disturbances a novel approach has been proposed which consists of a PID controller based on Mountain Gazelle Optimization (MGO) algorithm which is a newly introduced optimization algorithm and it is used to obtain the optimal gains of the PID controller in order to improve its performance under external disturbances since in such systems, any external disturbance or fault affects all the outputs. The proposed MGO-PID has same amount of inputs and outputs as the MIMO system.

articleTitle: Robust Control System Design for an Industrial Heavy Duty Gas Turbine under Network-Induced Imperfections
abstract: Advent of new communication technologies made it possible to replace point-to-point control structures with networked systems as a breakthrough toward Industry 4.0. However, overcoming communication imperfections is still a major issue. In this paper, a group of network-based cascade control systems is investigated in which, network communication is considered within the controller-actuator channel. In order to reduce conservatism and increase robustness of the control system, time-varying delay and packet dropouts are considered as separate terms using an augmented continuous-time state-space model. Based on Lyapunov theorem, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> stability conditions are attained dealing with external disturbances. An identified linear model for an industrial gas turbine unit is employed for performance assessment of the designed controllers. Obtained results confirm capability of the proposed method to achieve larger gain margins and more robustness against uncertain delays and data loss.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Nonlinear Observer for a Class of Applicable Nonlinear Systems
abstract: This article addresses the challenge of creating fixed-time observers for a specific class of nonlinear systems, containing both matched and mismatched uncertainties. The class of nonlinear systems discussed in this paper includes many real-world nonlinear systems such as unmanned aerial vehicles, robot manipulators, and so on, which makes the proposed observer applicable to many practical nonlinear systems. According to fixed time stability theorem, it is proven that states of proposed observer will achieve to the real states in a fixed time. Fixed-time observers offer a key advantage over finite-time observers: their convergence time is guaranteed regardless of the system's initial state; it solely depends on the design parameters. Numerical simulations confirm the proposed observer's ability to accurately estimate system states.

articleTitle: PCSA-TMRAM: Precharge Sense Amplifier-Based Ternary MRAM
abstract: Multi-valued logic is currently receiving much attention and has gained great importance. This paper discusses a novel approach to designing energy-efficient memory systems with high storage capacity using advanced multi-level logic. Due to increased power usage in existing ternary memory systems, the paper introduces a new ternary MRAM design. This design combines the energy-saving benefits of PCSA-based memory with the durable data retention of magnetic tunnel junctions, enhancing its application to ternary data processing. Using the 7nm FinFET technology for crafting digital circuits, the design significantly reduces energy consumption during reading and writing operations by up to 84% and 8%, respectively, compared to current ternary nonvolatile memories.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation and Analysis of a MIM Plasmonic Sensor Based on the Cross-Shaped Resonator
abstract: This study introduces a tunable plasmonic sensor. This sensor is built using metal-insulator-metal waveguides and its performance is analyzed, applying the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) approach. The sensor structure consists of a cross-shaped resonator with three stubs. The suggested sensor is a proper candidate for biosensor applications. It has a high refractive index sensitivity of 1390 nm/RIU and a great figure of merit of 61.72 RIU−1. Compared to other works reported in this literature, many of these values are the highest.

articleTitle: A Communication-Aware Scheduler for Containers in a Kubernetes Environment Using Girvan-Newman Clustering
abstract: Today, container technology has carved out a special place in cloud computing due to features such as ease of use and lower resource requirements compared to virtual machines. The issue of scheduling and mapping containers, which involves deciding which node each container should run on, is crucial due to its impact on resource efficiency and application performance. One of the main challenges in scheduling is managing the communications between containers. Placing containers on the appropriate node can reduce the latency in their communications or the volume of data transferred. In this study, a new approach to container scheduling based on a hierarchical clustering algorithm is proposed. The goal of this approach is to place containers that have a high volume of communication with each other in the same cluster, and then the algorithm tries to find a suitable node for placing this cluster. The results of implementing the proposed scheduler in a Kubernetes environment demonstrate a significant performance improvement, achieving a 2.62-fold increase compared to the default Kubernetes scheduler and a 2.66-fold improvement over a random scheduler. Additionally, the results indicate a decrease in data transfer volume between nodes and an increase within nodes.

articleTitle: Inversion Coefficient as a Key Design Parameter in MOS Device Performance
abstract: The paper discusses MOS device performance using the EKV model and its key parameter, the inversion coefficient (IC), for the 90nm CMOS process. The study includes sizing relationships, DC bias parameters, small signal parameters, gain and bandwidth relationships, gate referred thermal and flicker noise parameters, local area DC mismatch parameters, gate-source leakage current and figure of merit factors for low power RF designs. By using charts versus IC, the graphical view illustrates MOS performance tradeoffs. By introducing the MOSFET operating plane, optimal bias points for the best MOS performance can be selected. It is observed that the moderate inversion region is the most suitable for low-power design.

articleTitle: Improving the Performance and Robustness of Non-Minimum Phase Systems Using Integrated Feedforward-IMC Technique
abstract: For a non-minimum phase (NMP) quadruple tank process (QTP), a robust control design approach is suggested. To do this, concepts of robust, feedforward, and decoupling control techniques along with internal model control (IMC) are used together to improve the perfect tracking of the system. Then to cope with uncertainties, a centralized robust controller is synthesized. Appropriate weight functions are used to indicate the desired performance and uncertainty. Also, a comparison between using H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> mixed sensitivity and DK iteration robust controllers with the proposed approach is drawn in the literature. Numerical simulations are used to verify the effectiveness of the suggested design strategy, which is implemented to a QTP.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Model for House Number Detection and Recognition
abstract: Detection and recognition of information from natural images pose significant challenges in computer vision, with far-reaching implications for future applications. In recent years, the application of deep learning techniques to real-world image datasets has yielded notable achievements in the realms of recognition, detection, and pattern recognition. In this paper, we specifically tackle the challenge of number detection and recognition in real-world scenes by proposing deep learning models on the Street View House Numbers (SVHN) dataset. In the proposed models, to boost accuracy, we applied preprocessing steps to the training dataset. These steps included data augmentation techniques such as resizing, random rotation, random horizontal flip, angle degree changes, and optimization of hyperparameters and model layers. In the initial model, we utilized a fully connected Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model on sequences of digit images, achieving an impressive accuracy of 95 percent. Subsequently, a Convolutional-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) model was designed for temporal information modeling, utilizing a combination of CNN and LSTM layers that also achieved an accuracy of 93 percent. These models demonstrate high performance in recognizing numbers in complex and real-world environments. Our results underscore the significant enhancement in the accuracy of number recognition in real-world images achieved on the SVHN dataset by combining CNN models with data augmentation. We also compare the results of our proposed models with other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization of Spiral Antenna for Microwave Imaging Applications
abstract: This paper describes the application of multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) in the design of ultra-wideband equiangular spiral antennas for microwave imaging systems. The main goal of this design is to achieve enhanced time-domain pulse preservation in both main planes of the antenna. For the feeding structure, a microstrip to stripline balun is vertically connected to the arms of the spiral antenna from the back. Dimensions of the spiral antenna and its balun are both involved in optimization. The optimization results show that the fidelity factor higher than 0.98 in XY and higher than 0.8 in YZ-Planes is achieved, and the return loss is better than -10 dB at 3.1-10.6 GHz frequency band. Also, simulation results prove the capability of the proposed antenna in tumor detection.

articleTitle: Modeling and control of two PPR cooperative manipulations with a passive joint
abstract: In this academic study, we delve into a detailed analysis of the kinematic aspects of a collaborative manipulation utilizing two arms, aiming to move a long rod within a two-dimensional space. Each arm crucial to this task has two active principal joints and a passive revolute joint (PPR), strategically chosen to simplify and reduce the complexity of the system's equations. Additionally, this research explores the dynamics involved in this collaborative manipulation, examining the forces exerted while moving the rod. By addressing both kinematic and dynamic elements and proposing a non-linear control approach, this work significantly contributes to advancing cooperative robotic manipulation, especially in scenarios where strategic movement of elongated objects in a flat space is essential. this research is a simplified model of the movement of objects in 3D space by cooperative aerial manipulation and the passive joint mechanism is examined in it.

articleTitle: Denoising of the Diffusion Tensor Imaging Data Using k-Space Redundancy
abstract: Diffusion tensor imaging is a highly capable, yet noise-sensitive method for obtaining the brain's white matter structure. It comprises repeated acquisitions, each weighted by a diffusion gradient in one specific direction. The acquired data, therefore, has a large amount of redundancy that can be used for its efficient denoising. In this paper, we estimated the pattern for areas in the k-space most affected by the directional diffusion gradient. This pattern was then used for filtrating the acquired data for each direction. In particular, the areas minimally affected by diffusion gradients were replaced by the k-space data that was averaged over all directional acquisitions. The central idea for this filtering is the geometrical constraints on the diffusion caused by fiber orientations. This denoising approach was examined through the resulting reconstructed diffusion images as well as consequent fractional anisotropy (FA) maps, in terms of Signal-to-Noise Ratio and Contrast-to-Noise Ratio (CNR) obtained for different subsampling levels. The results demonstrated a 25.58% increase in SNR and a 27.86% increase in CNR for the FA map when our filter was applied during subsampling (44.44% of each k-space) in the datasets. Additionally, the qualitative assessment showed our filter resulted in a better representation of tracts in the FA map derived from the fully sampled k-spaces.

articleTitle: Improving Power Grid Operational Resilience During A Tornado Disaster
abstract: Managing energy and reducing load loss during extreme events in power systems, considering the uncertainty of element failures, presents significant challenges. This paper proposes the use of a Markov chain to predict element failures during extreme events. Optimal proactive optimization is then implemented for various event scenarios. The drawbacks associated with corrective strategies are discussed, emphasizing the importance of employing a proactive approach during such events and highlighting the benefits of system preparation. The IEEE 30 bus system, known for its complex mesh configuration, is used as a case study to demonstrate the method's effectiveness. The optimization problem is solved using GAMS software and the CPLEX solver. The obtained results underscore the significance of this approach.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Peer-to-Peer Transactions in Arizona State University's Microgrid by NSGA II
abstract: This study presents a novel approach to modeling and solving the multi-objective optimization problem of peer-to-peer transactions among agents within microgrids. A key innovation lies in considering each trade, including internal trades, as a decision variable, unlike prior research that focused on optimizing whole internal trades and grid exchanges. Using Arizona State University's microgrid as a case study with varying exchange rates, the study concludes that the proposed Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II with modified mutation outperforms existing studies by finding superior solutions in select scenarios, showcasing significant advancements in optimizing microgrid transactions.

articleTitle: Nonvolatile Quaternary Pre-Charged MRAM Cell Design based on Emerging Technologies
abstract: The remarkable attribute of multi-valued logic (MVL) in addressing the restriction of binary systems has spurred extensive research. Among various MVL types, quaternary logic exhibits greater compatibility with existing binary systems. The primary challenge in MVL lies in the hardware implementation of MVL circuits, which requires multi-threshold voltage transistors. Thanks to the nonvolatility feature of the magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) device, a nonvolatile quaternary pre-charged memory based on FinFET/MTJ and CNTFET/MTJ is proposed in this paper. Regarding both CNTFET and FinFET designs, simulation results report a great reduction of up to 80% in read delay and up to 97% in power delay product (PDP). Also, the CNTFET-based structure consumes up to 33% less static power compared to the previous designs.

articleTitle: Three-Leg AC/AC Converters:A Comprehensive Practical Overview
abstract: This paper focuses on examining and comparing several three-leg AC/AC converters. These converters, which utilize a three-leg topology, feature practical structures that enable the generation of a wide range of in-phase and out-of-phase outputs. Consequently, they find applications in various versatile scenarios, including constant voltage regulation (CVR), constant current regulation (CCR), dynamic voltage restorer (DVR), and even frequency conversion. After explaining the structure and operation of these converters, this paper will provide a comprehensive comparative evaluation, considering factors such as voltage gain, semiconductor switch count, quantity of passive components, switch current and voltage stress, and more. Ultimately, the paper will present the analytical conclusions drawn from these comparisons.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Fundamental Stock Prediction Using Companies' Financial Reports
abstract: Portfolio management is a key goal of investment. Therefore, a key factor in extremely successful revenues is the ability to predict shares and securities with efficiency. The use of fundamental stock analysis to forecast the long-term performance of shares is effective and potent. However, further investigation in this field suffers from the lack of online fundamental features. This paper proposes two approaches of time-dependent and independent stock prediction utilizing fundamental analysis. To accomplish this, we first present a brand-new fundamental feature dataset from TSE. Its features are extracted from corporate financial records, and each share's return and risk values serve as its prediction targets. Additionally, the impact of using temporal dependency-which is lacking from the great majority of machine learning techniques-on prediction performance is examined in this paper. Finally, we suggest using machine learning techniques and assess their effectiveness of fundamental stock prediction.

articleTitle: An Active Inductor-Based Differential Ring VCO with Wide Tuning Range for UWB Applications
abstract: In this paper, a wide band differential ring Voltage-Controlled Oscillator (VCO) using a composite load and dual-delay-path technique is presented. This topology consists of four delay stages connected in a ring structure. The proposed delay cell utilizes a pre-discharge path to output nodes to enhance the oscillation frequency. Also, a Lin-Payne active inductor as a composite is used load to provide a large tuning frequency range, while the differential topology of the cell improves the phase noise performance. The presented circuit is designed and simulated using standard 180 nm CMOS technology with a 1.8 V power supply (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf>). The center frequency of the proposed ring VCO is 3.5 GHz, and the output frequency of the signal can be varied from 1.87 GHz to 5.2 GHz (over a 3 GHz tuning range) by adjusting the control voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\text{Tun}\mathrm{e}})$</tex> from 1.3 V to 0 V. Over this range of frequency, the power consumption ranges from 0.77 mW to 2.84 mW, achieving a phase noise of −86.5 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz. The output oscillation signal swing ranges from 0.15 V to 1.55 V peak-to-peak, and the overall Figure of Merit (FoM) is −154.83 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz. Furthermore, corner, temperature, Monte Carlo, and other analyses have been conducted to demonstrate the reliability of the design.

articleTitle: Enhancing Precision in Dermoscopic Imaging using TransUNet and CASCADE
abstract: Medical imaging is advancing at a rapid pace, revolutionizing medicine. Automated skin lesion segmentation is vital for early skin cancer diagnosis, yet segmenting lesions in dermoscopic images presents considerable challenges. Despite recent good performance, CNN-based algorithms are unable to effectively learn explicit global and long-range semantic information because of the fundamental locality of convolution operations. The first medical image segmentation framework, TransUNet, was presented employing Vision Transformer as a strong encoder in a U-shaped architecture, in light of the growing interest in self-attention mechanisms in computer vision and their potential to address this issue. Using hierarchical vision transformers' multi-scale features, CASCADE is a novel attention-based decoder. The components of CASCADE are a convolutional attention module that improves the local and long-range context by suppressing background information and an attention gate that combines features. Using TransUNet's En-coder and CASCADE as the Decoder, the TransCASCADE model efficiently makes use of the global context stored by Transformers and detailed, high-resolution spatial information from CNN features. In this study, we utilized a novel optimizer called Lion to train our model, which improved memory efficiency, reduced complexity, and required fewer hyperparameters. Employing Lion resulted in superior performance compared to the base models. Experimental results demonstrate the high efficiency of the proposed method on PH2 dataset.

articleTitle: Employing Integrated Quantum Photonic Computers for Gaussian Boson Sampling
abstract: Gaussian boson sampling (GBS) is a tool for demonstrating quantum computational utilities and also exhibits mathematical connections to specific graph-related and quantum chemistry problems. It has been suggested that the samples generated from GBS could be utilized to improve stochastic algorithms in searching for certain graph features. In this study, we employed X8, a noisy intermediate-scale quantum computer, to address graph problems. The samples were produced from a 4-mode quantum photonic processor. This research represents a step toward analyzing Gaussian boson sampling as a tool for solving real-world problems using existing noisy intermediate-scale quantum computers and aims to encourage the development of quantum algorithms.

articleTitle: Efficient NVIS HF Hinged Half-Loop Vehicular Antenna Using Modal Analysis
abstract: This paper presents an efficient near vertical incidence skywave (NVIS) hinged half-loop vehicular antenna for high-frequency (HF) applications. The antenna consists of two main loops that play as the main radiating elements and also four smaller loops that both improve the antenna performance and help the dynamic performance of the overall structure under unwanted stress and road irregularities. The antenna arms are folded to completely cover an area as large as the roof of the car. We recognize suitable platform modes and ascertain practical methods for their excitation based on modal analysis. This approach enables a substantial increase in the antenna bandwidth in comparison to the isolated antenna system bandwidth at 25 MHz. Pattern and return loss of antenna are reported and at the conference further discussions related to tuning network and measurement will be illustrated.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Image Registration Using Fast Visual Saliency and Improved SIFT
abstract: Image registration is the matching process between two or more images at different times and by various sensors, in different imaging conditions and view angles. Scale-invariant feature transform (SIFT) is the benchmark algorithm for this registration. However, the algorithm is computationally expensive. In this article, a saliency detection method was proposed. The saliency detection method identifies the target area, and key points are extracted by SIFT algorithm in this area. The extraction of key points only in the target area causes the algorithm be fast as the valuable key points are extracted. The algorithm accuracy is suitable in comparison with the competing methods which makes the proposed saliency detection algorithm be a suitable choice in real-time applications. The employed descriptor is gradient local orientation histogram (GLOH). Finally, the pruning of the correct key points was performed by fast sample consensus (FSC) algorithm. Experiment results showed that the proposed method increased the computational efficiency by about 10% compared to other methods.

articleTitle: An Iterative Approach to Enhance the Accuracy of TDOA-Based Localization by Averaging and Reducing Noise
abstract: The Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) algorithm has become a popular localization method that offers promising results for passive scenarios. However, this algorithm may be significantly affected by noise, leading to high errors in estimating the position of the signal source; Nevertheless, a cumulative approach can help minimize its impact. In this study, we apply this idea to improve estimation accuracy. We have introduced an approach based on iterations of Chan's method. Also, the research thoroughly investigated and compared different TDOA methods, such as hyperbolic intersection, least squares (LS), and especially Chan. Through computer simulations, we found that this approach provides higher accuracy than other methods. After m iterations, the proposed method reduces Chan's estimation error by the square root factor of m.

articleTitle: Coherent Direction of Arrival Estimation using Multiple Toeplitz Space Time Spatial Smoothing
abstract: The direction of arrival (DOA) estimation task becomes more challenging when the sources are coherent. In this paper, a method has been suggested for the coherent DOA estimation. At first, the received signal of the uniform linear antenna array is divided into subarrays. For each of the subarrays, the multiple Toeplitz technique has been applied to produce the correlation matrix. Then, the forward backward smoothing has been exploited and the resultant correlation matrices are averaged over various snapshots to provide the improved-rank covariance matrix. At the last step, one of the subspace based DOA estimation schemes are leveraged to estimate the DOAs of the coherent sources. The simulation results indicate that the proposed method is superior over its rivals in various scenarios.

articleTitle: Electrical Properties of Dielectric Barrier Discharge Plasma Actuator in Argon with 13.56MHz RF Power Supply*
abstract: Dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) under atmospheric pressure has various industrial applications, and extensive academic research is now underway. Electrical characterization of the DBD actuator is critical for various reasons. This article describes numerous power calculation methods and compares them to determine the most accurate one. The voltage and current characteristics of the dielectric barrier discharge plasma in argon and a radio frequency power source at 13.56 megahertz, were measured, calculated input power, and compared to the theoretical technique to validate the measuring method and instruments. Finally, the power consumption of the plasma was determined from the Lissajous curve, with the capacitor monitor approach being the most accurate. The obtained power is consistent with the values provided in the articles.

articleTitle: Enhancing Brain Tumor Classification in OCT Images using Local Phase Quantization Features
abstract: Determining the boundary between healthy tissue and infiltrating tumors in brain tissue is considered one of the significant challenges for neurosurgeons. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) as a promising imaging modality provides fast and high-resolution imaging and offers a vital tool assisting surgeons in diagnosing the boundary of the brain tumor. However, interpreting OCT images is complex despite its advantages. Many studies have interpreted the information using intensity-based structural features. In this study, a proposed method aims to enhance diagnosis based on local phase quantization (LPQ) features. To the best of our knowledge, frequency-based features have not been utilized in any previous studies involving brain tumor classification with OCT images. Additionally, a K-means algorithm has been employed to identify regions of interest (ROI) with high SNR in OCT images automatically in contrast to threshold-based methods which are highly dependent on a set of parameters. The dataset comprises B-scans from 15 different patients, selected from regions with tumor infiltration exceeding 60% (WM>60%) and healthy tissues (WM0%) in the white matter region. The results were achieved by utilizing an SVM classifier and employing adaptive synthetic sampling (ADASYN), coupled with grid-search cross-validation (Grid-SCV), to address data imbalance and optimize model parameters. The results, validated based on the accuracy (AC), sensitivity (SE), and specificity (SP), reached 98.53%, 98.14%, and 98.88%, respectively outperformed previous works and highlighted its potential as a computational diagnostic tool.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Refractive Index Sensor Using a Metal-Insulator-Metal Waveguide with a Disk-Shaped Cavity and Silver Nanorod Defects
abstract: A plasmonic refractive index (RI) sensor is simulated using a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) waveguide with a disk-shaped cavity containing silver nanorod defects. The dielectric inside the cavity has an RI of 1.3, close to the RI of glucose. The results indicate an RI sensitivity of 1242.86 nm per RI unit (RIU) and a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 76 nm. This article also demonstrates the capability to measure blood glucose concentration, with a glucose sensitivity of 0.146 nm.L.g-1. The sensor is well-suited for applications in medicine, photonics, and optoelectronics.

articleTitle: A New LDO Regulator with Adaptive PSR Improvement Under Wide Load Current Range and Fast Load Transient Response
abstract: This paper presents a novel off-chip capacitor-less LDO with high PSR from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40\mu \mathrm{A}$</tex> to 45mA load current range. Changing the load current in conventional LDOs causes a variation in the output resistance of the LDO and moves the pole located at the pass transistor's gate terminal. These changes result in the PSR degradation at some load current ranges, in such a way the LDO cannot satisfy the required PSR at the whole load current range. The proposed LDO provides an adaptive feed-forward path to improve the PSR at the entire load current ranges. The transfer function of the proposed feed-forward path has a zero with a specific gain, that is skillfully shifted by the amount of output resistance and the pole positioned at the gate terminal of the pass transistor. This method leads to enhancing PSR across the entire load current spectrum. According to simulation findings for the suggested LDO in TSMC 180 nm CMOS technology, the output PSR reaches −60 dB at 13 kHz across the entire load current range. The proposed LDO operates without requiring an external off-chip capacitor, exhibiting a quiescent current of 900nA and a phase margin of 54 degrees within an input voltage range of 1.8 to 2.3 volts.

articleTitle: Accurate Methods for Automatic Detection of Characteristic Points in Electrocardiograms
abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is a widely used technique for recording the electrical activity of the heart. Automatic identification of ECG characteristic points (fiducial points) is essential for cardiac diseases diagnosis. In the present study, the characteristic points including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> peak, isoelectric level, S peak, J point, P peak and onset, offset and peak of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> wave are investigated. We attempted to employ an approach to detect each of the ECG characteristic points with acceptable accuracy. The strategy developed to identify the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> peak involves a preprocessing stage on the basis of Shannon energy envelope technique, followed by a phase of peak-detection logic utilizing the Hilbert transform. After calculating the angle of the points following <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> peak, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> peak and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> point were found. This paper represents a sliding area which is covered by the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> wave curve to determine offset of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> wave, and then peak and onset of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> wave could be identified by offset of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> wave. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> peak detection is practically analogous to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> peak detection. After calculating the angle of the points following the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> peak, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> peak and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> point were found. to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> peak detection. The characteristic points detection methods were validated using MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm, Long Term ST database, as well as European ST-T database, and total accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$98.26\%$</tex> was achieved.

articleTitle: Cooperative Coverage Path Planning Using Q-Learning and Sarsa in Two Environments
abstract: This paper presents the coverage environment by multi agents using reinforcement learning with Q-learning and Sarsa algorithms. Two environments are explored to study cooperative coverage path planning with these algorithms. The goal is to achieve coverage in the environment by having agents collaborate to reduce energy consumption. Initially, an obstacle-free environment is examined, then an obstacle is considered in the environment. The proposed algorithm involves sharing experiences among agents to cover environments containing obstacles, and compares its convergence speed to scenarios without sharing experiences. The proposed algorithm's performance is assessed through different simulations.

articleTitle: A New High Step-Up Quasi Z-Source DC-DC Converter Using Buffer and Switched Capacitor Techniques
abstract: In this paper, a new high step-up quasi-Z-source DC-DC converter is introduced using a buffer section and a switched capacitor cell. The buffer section and the switched capacitor are added to extend the basic quasi-Z-source DC-DC converter to achieve a higher voltage gain with a continuous input current with the same voltage stress on semiconductors and capacitors. The proposed converter constitutes one switch and 4 diodes, implying two more semiconductors compared to the basic quasi-Z-source DC-DC converter. The performance analysis, the steady state and theoretical equations, the comparison and components design are derived and verified by simulation waveforms. The components are designed for a 400 W converter power, and the simulations are carried out in the PSIM software.

articleTitle: Adaptive Smooth Super Twisting Sliding Mode Control for Parkinson's Tremor Treatment
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common disease associated with prominent symptoms such as hand tremors and muscular rigidity. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a commonly used therapy for alleviating the symptoms of that condition. Implementing a closed-loop control system for DBS that applies a basal ganglia (BG) model is a common method for tremor determination in Parkinson's patients. In order to reduce Parkinson's tremor and decrease the necessary amount of stimulation, this work details the successful simultaneous control of two regions inside the BG, specifically the subthalamic nucleus (STN) and the globus pallidus internal (GPi). A partial state feedback (PSF) controller is used to stimulate the GPi, while an adaptive smooth super twisting sliding mode controller (ASSTSMC) is used to stimulate STN. According to the results of the simulation, the proposed method is superior and more successful than adaptive sliding mode control.

articleTitle: Second-Order Sliding Mode Control for DC-DC Buck Converter with Input Voltage Ripple Elimination
abstract: In this paper, a second-order sliding mode controller is proposed for the DC-DC buck converter. The proposed SOSMC scheme has been developed to reduce the voltage ripple in the output rectifier stage, improve the control system robustness, and guarantee finite-time convergence properties under load variations and parameter uncertainties. Also, the capability of the proposed controller is verified and compared with the other sliding mode controllers using the MATLAB/Simulink toolbox. To evaluate the performance of this control system, three different cases are studied: response to start-up, turbulence in load, and change in reference voltage level. The results show that the proposed SOSMC eliminates the voltage ripple, improves the steady-state error, and reduces the settling time of the output voltage.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis of Power Production and Efficiency in Shahid Mofateh Hamedan Power Plant: A Comparative Study of Operational Indicators
abstract: The aging of thermal power plants, the lack of precise monitoring of power plant operations, and, at times, the sole prioritizing of generation capacity in thermal power plants have brought about significant noticeable changes in their operational conditions over time. In this regard, one of the points of view that can evaluate the operational status of a thermal power plant is to identify and examine the operation indicators of that power plant and calculate the sensitivity of production power and efficiency to these indicators. In determining the reference indicators at the Shahid Mofateh power plant, first, the power plant operation indicators are identified based on the design documents or the initial operation of the power plant; in a field operation program in the power plant, the values ​​of the relevant indicators have been collected or measured. Analyzing the differences created in the indicators compared to the design conditions, using the modeling tools of Thermoflow software, prioritizing the indicators, and taking into account some assumptions have led to the determination of new reference indicators in the Shahid Mofateh power plant.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Coverage Path Planning for Multi-Agent Systems with ACO and GA
abstract: Coverage path planning (CPP) is a vital task in various fields, including agriculture, robotics, and unmanned aerial vehicles. It involves determining a path that covers all points of a given area while avoiding obstacles and minimizing overlapping. This paper presents a comprehensive approach to CPP that consists of two main phases: formation and coverage. Agents are divided into several groups, and each group reaches a consensus to establish a specific formation at a rendezvous point. Then Based on the agreed-upon location, a specific area is assigned to each group for coverage. For this purpose, first, the Voronoi division of the coverage space is done through triangular meshing then the scanning time of Voronoi cells by each group and the migration time of each group from its initial position to the destination cell have been utilized for region allocation. Finally, the Traveling Salesman Problem is tackled using ant colony and genetic algorithms to find the order of visitation for each group of agents. In this paper, obstacles have been considered in the cost function for both ant colony optimization and genetic algorithm, resulting in the optimal solution for the order of visitation for each group of agents. In addition, the proposed coverage path planning (CPP) method utilizes heterogeneous coverage to provide fast and effective coverage. The use of multiple agents covering their own areas ensures that if one agent fails, the mission does not stop, increasing the mission's strength and robustness.

articleTitle: Outage Analysis of Distributed Relying NOMA in Cognitive Radio Networks
abstract: We introduce the application of Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) to a cooperative cognitive radio network. Our study focuses on a two-stage cooperative scheme where a secondary transmitter can simultaneously transmit with a primary transmitter using uplink NOMA. We propose a distributed cooperative NOMA scheme that facilitates the simultaneous forwarding of superimposed signals to the respective destinations by K relays. Our analysis delves into the outage probability and diversity order of both the primary and secondary users. We show that the proposed scheme's performance is improved by utilizing multiple relays. Ultimately, we validate the theoretical results through simulations.

articleTitle: A Novel Tunable LC Filter for Ultra High Frequency Applications
abstract: A novel LC filter is proposed in this paper. The proposed structure consists of a square spiral inductor with a tunable capacitor. The outer turn of the inductor is also a part of the capacitor. The capacitor is designed using floating technique to get high quality factor (570-690). The size of designed filter is 1.4×1.2 mm2. Tuning range of the filter is 35%. The maximum quality factor of the filter is 118. the insertion loss is about −1db and the return loss is equal to −27db and −25db in pass frequency of 5.8GHz-6.8GHz.

articleTitle: Angular Stable Multiband Miniaturized Flexible Frequency Selective Surface
abstract: This paper presents a multiband miniaturized flexible frequency selective surface (FSS) with a high angularity. The proposed single-layer FSS tessellates with subwavelength hexagonal unit cells using miniaturized meandered arms with inclination angle of 120°. Results exhibit four frequency bands of 2.6-4.45 GHz (52.5%), 5.25-5.65 GHz (7.4%), 6.55-6.85 GHz (4.5%), and 7.8-8.05 GHz (3.3%). The designed FSS shows a low transmission loss at the pass bands, a low substrate thickness, and a stable angular response. At the conference, details of the design steps, circuit mode analysis, and performances for different radii of curvatures will be introduced.

articleTitle: A Bidirectional Transformerless Direct AC-AC Dynamic Voltage Restorer with Extended Compensation Range and Up/Down Capability
abstract: The primary focus of this article is on enhancing the performance of direct AC/AC converters for their application in Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) through modifications in the configuration of the AC/AC converter interconnection. In the proposed configuration, contrary to conventional setups, the converter's input power is supplied from the load side and applied in series to the grid. This arrangement allows for a substantial increase in the compensating range of the DVR without the need for alterations in the circuit topology of the AC/AC converter. Following the introduction of the converter circuit topology, the proposed configuration is presented. The theoretical analysis is then elaborated, and finally, the presented theory is validated through simulating the converter's performance in condition of 30% voltage sag and 30% voltage swell for DVR application under a 2KW load.

articleTitle: Optimization of Fifth Order Band-Pass Ladder Filter and Statistical Analysis of Reverse Problem
abstract: In this article, elements of a fifth order ladder type filter circuit are found through optimization, and circuits having optimum or near optimum responses statistically analyzed. Algorithms used for optimization are: GA, PSO, TLBO and combinations of GA with two others. In addition, a modified version of PSO-GA is introduced for multi-modal optimization and results shown. At last, PSO-GA algorithm along with a parameter change technique is used to find distribution of elements around optimum point.

articleTitle: Three Improved Boost Topologies with Continuous Input/Output Currents Suitable for High-Voltage Applications
abstract: This paper proposes a family of non-isolated high-gain DC-DC converters that have these merits: (i) both the input and output currents are continuous, and the input/output filter capacitors experience less current stress; (ii) the load-source common ground has been provided; (iii) only one switch has been employed in the proposed topologies which increases its reliability; (iv) the employed switch in the topologies is low-sided which leads to its easy drive circuit; (v) higher voltage gains are accessible with lower duty cycle percentages; (vi) the semiconductors experience low voltage/current stresses that lead to high efficiency. The proposed topologies are discussed in both ideal/non-ideal modes. This family can be a suitable base for the other improved topologies. This concept is the same as Luo converters, which are the fundamental part of lots of non-isolated topologies. Finally, the simulation results from PLECS are presented.

articleTitle: Design of Fresnel-Region Millimeter-Wave Metasurface Beam Shaper Using Deep Learning
abstract: In this paper, we present a new approach for designing a metasurface structure that leverages deep learning techniques for beam shaping a millimeter-wave source in the Fresnel region. The selection of unit cell geometry is crucial to attain accurate control over the phasefront of the incident wave. We show that our selection of unit cells enables the metasurface to produce the desired beam intensity on the target plane. We generate 61,000 datasets using analytical solutions of the beam shaping problem and train our neural network with an average loss of lower than 2%. The efficiency of our suggested method is evaluated by designing the phase profile of the metasurface to generate flat-top irradiation at a specific distance from the metasurface. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed deep learning approach for designing beam shaper metasurfaces.

articleTitle: A New Double Rotor Switched Reluctance Motor Aiming at Average Torque Improvement
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-rotor segmental switched reluctance motor. Permanent magnets are embedded between the stator segments to increase the flux density in the air gap. The stator part of the proposed motor is filled with an alloy of non-magnetic material. For greater strength of the parts at the ends of the segments, a stator has been created for better locking. The proposed motor has been fed through four phases, by using finite element analysis software The characteristic of static torque at rated current has been compared with the conventional rotor sample, which has strengthened the average torque and increased the maximum torque.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a TEM Double-Ridge Horn Antenna for Ultra-Wideband Applications
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-wideband, robust, low-cost double-ridge horn antenna (DRHA). As the frequency rises above 12 GHz, the typical DRHA radiation patterns lose their ability to maintain favorable properties in the frequency band; the level of the main lobes split, and the value of the gain decreases. The configuration of the antenna may be significantly impacted by the spaces between internal structures, particularly those created in the part of the feeding. The proposed antenna can achieve excellent radiation characteristics across the 0.7 to 18 GHz frequency range. Its gain ranges from 8.3 to 17.8 dBi and enhances noticeably and consistently in the entire high-frequency band and also the value of the VSWR is less than 2. The design procedure and all the dimensions of these antennas are given, along with the simulated and measured results. It is important to note that good agreement between them has been observed.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a DC-DC Dual-Input Single-Output Topology for Renewable Energy Applications
abstract: The principal objective of proposing multi-input DC-DC converters, is to compound several types of sources, or a number of PV modules to provide the demanded load. A DC-DC dual-input non-isolated boost converter is proposed in this paper. The operation of the topology in continuous conduction modes and the related calculations are assessed and presented. The performance of the converter is compared other dual-input topologies to investigate the exclusivities. The validity of the presented structure is verified by simulation and inquiring the circuit using PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Total Transfer Capability Improvement Using High Temperature Low Sag Conductors
abstract: Total transfer capability (TTC), which is a key factor in the nowadays deregulated power systems, is usually restricted by the overloaded transmission lines. High temperature low sag (HTLS) conductors can increase transmission lines thermal limits and can be considered as a promising solution for improving TTC. There are several types of HTLS conductors with different characteristics which can be utilized for upgrading existing transmission networks transfer capabilities. This paper presents an algorithm for improving TTC using HTLS conductors. This algorithm identifies the transmission lines that restrict the TTC level and evaluates various HTLS conductors for installation at these lines using analytical hierarchical process (AHP) method by taking into account the economic and technical viewpoints. The process of calculation of TTC is done using optimal power flow (OPF) method in the GAMS software. Numerical studies are conducted using IEEE 9-bus and 24-bus test systems and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in increasing the TTC level.

articleTitle: A New High Voltage Gain Non-Isolated DC-DC Converter
abstract: This research presents a novel DC-DC converter intended for distribution systems based on interleaved technique. This design incorporates a built-in transformer (BIT), coupled inductors (CIs), a switched capacitor (SC) technique, and voltage multiplier cells (VMCs). Among the outstanding features of the alliance of these elements, we can mention high voltage gain, high power density, and reduction of the voltage stress of the elements by increasing the turn ratio CIs or BIT and the ability to adjust the turn ratio to enhance voltage gain. It also reduces the components’ current stress and the incoming current's ripple value. In this converter, the leakage energy is recycled. These innovations substantially improve the overall efficiency of the system. The reduced voltage stress allows for low-voltage rate switches, which reduces conduction losses and costs. It is discussed in detail how the converter operates and its characteristics. A simulation with input/output voltage 20V and 800V, respectively, is developed to verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: An Improved U-Type Inter-Modular Biased-Flux Permanent Magnet Motor
abstract: This paper proposes an improved inter-modular permanent magnet (IMPM) motor where the PMs are effectively splitted in a way that the air-gap harmonics are manipulated. The torque ripple of the proposed structure is greatly reduced and the magneto motive force throughout the air-gap experiences more transition under stator side teeth. The operation principle of the proposed structure is explored and it is compared with the IMPM motor. Moreover, it is explained how the proposed structure still maintains the cooling vents that are available in the IMPM topology. The efficiency and power factor of the proposed structure is also improved. It has been investigated that the addition of a flux bridge above the PMs will substantially decrease the demagnetization of the PMs. The over-load capability of the two structures are almost the same. The results of the simulation section are obtained through two-dimensional finite element method (2-D FEM).

articleTitle: A New Method Based on Empirical Wavelet Transform in Order to Detect Current Transformer Saturation in Distance Relay
abstract: Current Transformers (CT) used to protect power systems generally use a ferromagnetic core. Therefore, they are subject to magnetic saturation, which occurs due to residual flux remaining in the core before a fault occurs. When a current transformer saturates, its current waveform changes. This can cause the protective relays to malfunction. Most protection relays have saturation current compensation to estimate the actual current. In addition, some protection relays change their calculations during CT saturation. All of these cases depend on CT saturation detection. For this reason, a CT saturation detection algorithm based on the empirical wavelet transform (EWT) signal decomposition method is presented in this article. The presented method was tested with the software DIg SILENT and MATLAB in an IEEE 39 bus standard network. The simulation results demonstrate that the presented method has exceptional performance at CT saturation for all types of defects and also for noisy signals.

articleTitle: Sliding-mode $H_{\infty}$ Control of Continuous Singular Systems under Zeno-free Event-triggered Sampling Scheme
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of event-triggered sliding mode control for linear singular systems. The objective is to develop a sliding mode control law using an event-triggered sampling scheme that ensures the E-UUB admissibility of the singular system with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> performance. To achieve this, we propose a novel Zeno-free event-triggered condition for detecting the sampling time instants. Additionally, we introduce an integral sliding surface and establish sufficient conditions to guarantee the admissibility of the sliding dynamic. The design parameters associated with the event-triggered sampling scheme and sliding surface are determined by solving linear matrix inequalities, which can be conveniently solved using MATLAB software. The event-triggered sliding mode controller is specifically developed to guide the system trajectories towards the sliding surface within a finite time. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed controller are validated through simulation results obtained from an illustrative example.

articleTitle: HyperSpectral Image Classification Using an 3D Convolutional Mixer Block
abstract: HyperSpectral Image (HSI) processing has many applications in agriculture, Earth Change Monitoring, etc. Classification of HSIs is an important stage in most applications. Recently transformers have shown outstanding performance in computer vision tasks and some transformer-based methods have been introduced for HSI classification. In this paper, we propose a novel classification algorithm using the convolutional mixer for HSI classification. Convolutional mixer is similar to transformers and is used to mix spatial and spectral information which are gathered separately by using depth wise convolution followed by a point wise convolution. We have used 3D convolutions in mixer block due to the 3D shape of hyperspectral cuboids to extract spectral and spatial features simultaneously, which have not been done before, to the best of our knowledge.
